warnings: This release was made from a working tree with uncommitted changes, so what shipped and what is in git are not the same thing. The reference points at what was actually checked.
summary: tiny-greeter shipped a54e4cd. What "working" means did NOT move: The last check on 1.0.0 with uncommitted changes left 1 difference unaccounted for. Checks of tiny-greeter go on comparing against 1.0.0, the build shipped on 2026-10-03 — that is still the standard, so a regression this release introduced would be reported rather than adopted.
lines: tiny-greeter shipped at commit a54e4cd. There was no new tag, no version bump and no npm publish to go on, so this is being recorded as the release because somebody said it shipped.

The reference did NOT move. Refusing to make 1.0.0 with uncommitted changes the standard for tiny-greeter: the last check left 1 difference nobody accounted for, 1 of which is in a class nobody may wave through. Cutting a broken build as the standard is how a safety net silently becomes a rubber stamp: from tomorrow the tool would call this behaviour correct, stop reporting it, and go on quietly passing every run that keeps it broken. Fix them, or force the cut and accept that it is recorded as forced with the reason above kept beside it.
Your release is unaffected — this only decides what future checks compare against.
